subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: How should maintainers split the remaining umbrella work across dashboard auth persistence, Codex/OpenAI OAuth propagation, installer/runtime compatibility, and session completion/context hygiene?
rationale: The requested end state crosses security-sensitive credential behavior, setup UX, provider routing, package/update guarantees, and session-runtime contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the ownership or persistence model.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split focused work
options.body: Use this issue as coordination context while routing each narrow subproblem to its owner and closing it only after the active subpaths are landed or explicitly rejected.

options.title: Promote one canonical subtrack
options.body: Choose a narrower existing issue as canonical for the remaining work and update this issue to point there if maintainers want less umbrella tracking.

options.title: Sponsor one coordinated project
options.body: Treat this as a planned cross-area reliability project with explicit auth/security, installer, runtime, and session-state owners before implementation.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split focused work
recommendation.body: Use this issue as coordination context while routing each narrow subproblem to its owner and closing it only after the active subpaths are landed or explicitly rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: Current inspected blame and docs/runtime history touch the broadest set of affected surfaces under one routing candidate.
